title: Korean War — US Leads UN Coalition
description: North Korea's invasion of South Korea prompted the United States to lead a UN coalition to defend the South, marking the first major armed confrontation of the Cold War. The NSC-68 strategy paper simultaneously committed the US to a massive military buildup.

title: Truman Orders Hydrogen Bomb Development
description: President Truman ordered the Atomic Energy Commission to accelerate development of the hydrogen bomb in response to the Soviet Union's first nuclear test in 1949. The decision marked a fateful escalation of the nuclear arms race.

title: Truman Fires General MacArthur
description: President Truman relieved General Douglas MacArthur of command after MacArthur publicly contradicted administration policy on the Korean War. The episode established a landmark precedent for civilian control of the military.

title: Japanese Peace Treaty and US-Japan Security Alliance
description: The United States and 48 other nations signed a peace treaty formally ending World War II with Japan and simultaneously established a bilateral US-Japan security alliance. The treaty restored Japanese sovereignty and anchored the Pacific security order.

title: Korean War Armistice Signed
description: An armistice agreement ended active combat in the Korean War, establishing the demilitarized zone near the 38th parallel after roughly 36,000 American deaths. The war ended in a stalemate with Korea permanently divided.

title: CIA Orchestrates Iranian Coup
description: The CIA and British intelligence organized Operation Ajax, overthrowing Iranian Prime Minister Mosaddegh and restoring Shah Pahlavi to power. The operation had lasting consequences for US-Iran relations and established a template for Cold War covert intervention.

title: Brown v. Board of Education Ruling
description: The Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional, overturning the 1896 Plessy v. Ferguson doctrine of separate but equal. The ruling launched the legal dismantling of Jim Crow segregation.

title: Senate Censures McCarthy — Red Scare Ends
description: The US Senate voted 67-22 to censure Senator Joseph McCarthy, effectively ending the anti-Communist witch-hunts known as McCarthyism. The episode illustrated both the dangers and institutional limits of political demagoguery.

title: Interstate Highway Act Signed
description: President Eisenhower signed the Federal Aid Highway Act, authorizing construction of 41,000 miles of interstate highways in the largest public works project in US history. The system transformed American transportation, suburban development, and economic geography.

title: Suez Crisis — US Forces Allied Withdrawal
description: The United States pressured Britain, France, and Israel to withdraw from their military operation against Egypt during the Suez Crisis. The episode asserted American dominance over its Cold War allies and reshaped the post-colonial international order.

title: Eisenhower Deploys Troops to Enforce Little Rock Desegregation
description: President Eisenhower sent federal troops to Little Rock, Arkansas, to enforce school desegregation after Governor Faubus used the National Guard to block nine Black students. The decision established federal supremacy over states in civil rights enforcement.

title: NASA Created — Space Race Launched
description: Congress established the National Aeronautics and Space Administration in response to the Soviet Sputnik launch, centralizing US civilian space exploration. NASA set the institutional foundation for the Apollo program and America's Space Race competition.

title: U-2 Spy Plane Incident Derails Superpower Summit
description: A US U-2 spy plane was shot down over the Soviet Union and pilot Francis Gary Powers was captured, derailing a planned Eisenhower-Khrushchev summit. The incident severely damaged superpower relations and exposed the scale of US aerial surveillance.

title: Bay of Pigs Invasion Fails
description: A CIA-trained force of Cuban exiles attempted to invade Cuba and overthrow Castro at the Bay of Pigs but was quickly defeated. The fiasco embarrassed the Kennedy administration and strengthened Castro's position, shaping a decade of US-Cuba confrontation.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
description: The discovery of Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba brought the US and USSR to the brink of nuclear war for 13 days. Kennedy's naval blockade and secret diplomacy resolved the crisis and established nuclear crisis management norms that defined the Cold War.

title: Kennedy Assassinated — Johnson Assumes Presidency
description: President John F. Kennedy was shot and killed in Dallas, Texas, on November 22, 1963, and Lyndon Johnson was immediately sworn in. The transition set the stage for the sweeping Great Society legislation that followed.

title: Limited Nuclear Test Ban Treaty Signed
description: The United States, Soviet Union, and United Kingdom signed the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty, prohibiting nuclear weapon testing in the atmosphere, outer space, and underwater. It was the first significant arms control agreement of the Cold War era.

title: Civil Rights Act of 1964 Signed
description: President Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, outlawing discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin in employment and public accommodations. It was the most significant civil rights legislation since Reconstruction.

title: Gulf of Tonkin Resolution — Vietnam War Authorization
description: Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, giving President Johnson broad authority to escalate US military involvement in Vietnam without a formal declaration of war. It became the legal basis for America's most costly Cold War conflict.

title: Voting Rights Act Signed
description: President Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act, outlawing discriminatory voting practices that had disenfranchised Black voters across the South for generations. The act transformed American democracy by enfranchising millions and enabling new political representation.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Created
description: President Johnson signed legislation establishing Medicare for the elderly and Medicaid for low-income Americans. The programs represented the most significant expansion of the US social safety net since Social Security and remain cornerstones of American healthcare.

title: Tet Offensive Transforms Vietnam War
description: The Viet Cong's massive Tet Offensive shocked Americans who had been told the US was winning in Vietnam, destroying public confidence in Johnson's war strategy. The offensive forced Johnson's decision not to seek reelection and transformed the political debate.

title: Fair Housing Act Passed
description: Congress passed the Fair Housing Act prohibiting discrimination in the sale, rental, and financing of housing. Enacted days after King's assassination, it was the last major legislative achievement of the civil rights movement era.

title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
description: Astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the moon on July 20, 1969. The achievement fulfilled Kennedy's challenge and represented the pinnacle of the Space Race, demonstrating US technological supremacy.

title: US Invades Cambodia — Kent State Killings Follow
description: President Nixon ordered US and South Vietnamese forces to invade Cambodia to attack North Vietnamese sanctuaries. The incursion provoked massive domestic protests including the Kent State shootings, in which National Guard soldiers killed four students.

title: Nixon Ends Dollar's Gold Convertibility — Nixon Shock
description: President Nixon ended the convertibility of US dollars to gold, effectively ending the Bretton Woods international monetary system. The Nixon Shock transformed global currency markets and ended the postwar financial order.

title: Pentagon Papers Published
description: The New York Times and Washington Post published the classified Pentagon Papers, revealing decades of government deception about the Vietnam War. The Supreme Court upheld the newspapers' right to publish, establishing a landmark First Amendment precedent.

title: Nixon Opens Diplomatic Relations with China
description: President Nixon made a historic visit to the People's Republic of China, ending 23 years of diplomatic isolation and opening relations with Beijing. The visit was a major geopolitical realignment that reshaped the Cold War balance of power.

title: Watergate Break-in Begins Constitutional Crisis
description: Operatives connected to the Nixon reelection campaign were arrested for breaking into the Democratic National Committee headquarters at the Watergate complex. The subsequent cover-up set off the gravest constitutional crisis since the Civil War.

title: Vietnam Peace Accords Signed
description: The Paris Peace Accords ended direct US military involvement in Vietnam after more than a decade of combat and approximately 58,000 American deaths. The agreement was a face-saving exit, with South Vietnam falling to North Vietnam two years later.

title: Arab Oil Embargo Triggers Energy Crisis
description: Arab OPEC members imposed an oil embargo on the US in response to American support for Israel in the Yom Kippur War, quadrupling oil prices and causing severe fuel shortages. The crisis transformed US energy policy and accelerated the end of cheap oil.

title: Nixon Resigns Presidency Over Watergate
description: Facing near-certain impeachment, Richard Nixon became the first and only US president to resign from office after the Supreme Court ordered him to release tape recordings proving his role in the cover-up. The resignation ended the gravest constitutional crisis of the 20th century.

title: Fall of Saigon Ends Vietnam War
description: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon, completing the conquest of South Vietnam and ending the Vietnam War. The dramatic helicopter evacuations symbolized American defeat and defined a generation's reckoning with US military limits.

title: Carter Signs Panama Canal Treaties
description: President Carter signed treaties with Panama agreeing to transfer control of the Canal Zone by December 31, 1999. The controversial decision improved US relations with Latin America and acknowledged the limits of informal empire.

title: Camp David Accords Broker Israeli-Egyptian Peace
description: President Carter brokered a historic peace framework between Egyptian President Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Begin at Camp David. The accords led to the first peace treaty between Israel and an Arab state, fundamentally reshaping Middle Eastern diplomacy.

title: Iran Hostage Crisis Begins
description: Iranian students seized the US Embassy in Tehran and took 52 American diplomats hostage, beginning a 444-day ordeal that consumed the Carter presidency. A failed military rescue deepened the humiliation and contributed decisively to Carter's 1980 defeat.

title: Volcker Shock — Fed Raises Interest Rates Sharply
description: Federal Reserve Chairman Paul Volcker raised interest rates dramatically to combat double-digit inflation, sending them above 20 percent by 1981. The resulting deep recession ultimately broke inflation and shaped the economic landscape of the Reagan era.

title: Carter Responds to Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan
description: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan prompted President Carter to impose sanctions, boycott the Moscow Olympics, and begin arming the Afghan mujahideen through Operation Cyclone. The US response effectively ended détente and triggered the final phase of Cold War confrontation.

title: Reagan Tax Cuts — Economic Recovery Tax Act
description: Reagan signed a sweeping tax cut package reducing the top marginal income tax rate from 70 to 50 percent. It was the largest tax cut in US history at the time and launched the supply-side economic experiment that defined the Reagan era.

title: Marine Barracks Bombing in Beirut
description: A suicide truck bomb destroyed the US Marine barracks in Beirut, killing 241 American service members in the deadliest terrorist attack on US forces to that point. Reagan subsequently withdrew troops, establishing a pattern of response to asymmetric terrorism.

title: Iran-Contra Affair Exposed
description: Reagan administration officials secretly sold arms to Iran and used the proceeds to fund Nicaraguan Contra rebels in defiance of a congressional ban. The scandal was the gravest political crisis of the Reagan presidency and raised fundamental questions about executive accountability.

title: INF Treaty Eliminates Nuclear Missiles in Europe
description: Reagan and Soviet leader Gorbachev signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, eliminating an entire class of nuclear weapons for the first time. The treaty marked the beginning of the end of the Cold War arms race.

title: Americans with Disabilities Act Signed
description: President Bush signed the Americans with Disabilities Act, prohibiting discrimination against people with disabilities in employment, transportation, and public accommodations. It was the most sweeping disability rights law in US history.

title: Gulf War — Operation Desert Storm Liberates Kuwait
description: A US-led coalition launched a massive air and ground offensive that liberated Kuwait from Iraqi occupation in 100 hours of ground combat. The victory restored American military confidence after Vietnam and established the model for large-scale coalition warfare.

title: NAFTA Passed by Congress
description: Congress approved the North American Free Trade Agreement, creating a free trade zone among the United States, Canada, and Mexico. NAFTA became one of the most consequential and politically divisive trade agreements in US history.

title: Dayton Accords End Bosnian War
description: The Dayton Peace Agreement, brokered by the United States, ended the Bosnian War and established the framework for post-conflict Bosnia. The agreement required 60,000 NATO troops and demonstrated American willingness to lead European security.

title: Clinton Reelected — Welfare Reform Signed
description: President Clinton signed welfare reform legislation ending the federal entitlement to welfare and establishing work requirements, while winning reelection over Republican Bob Dole. The reforms reflected Clinton's 'Third Way' centrism and transformed American social policy.

title: Clinton Impeached by House of Representatives
description: The House impeached President Clinton on charges of perjury and obstruction of justice related to the Lewinsky affair. The Senate acquitted him in February 1999, but the episode permanently polarized partisan politics.

title: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Repeals Glass-Steagall
description: Congress repealed the Glass-Steagall Act separating commercial and investment banking, allowing financial institutions to offer combined services. Many economists later cited this deregulation as a contributing factor to the 2008 financial crisis.

title: Bush Wins Disputed Presidential Election
description: George W. Bush defeated Al Gore in the most controversial presidential election in modern history, decided by 537 votes in Florida after the Supreme Court halted the recount. Gore won the popular vote, reshaping perceptions of American electoral legitimacy.

title: September 11 Terrorist Attacks
description: Al-Qaeda hijackers crashed four commercial airliners into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and a Pennsylvania field, killing nearly 3,000 people. The attacks were the deadliest in world history and permanently transformed American foreign and domestic policy.

title: War in Afghanistan Begins
description: The United States invaded Afghanistan to destroy Al-Qaeda and overthrow the Taliban government that harbored them. Operation Enduring Freedom began on October 7, 2001, launching America's longest war at nearly 20 years.

title: USA PATRIOT Act Dramatically Expands Surveillance
description: Congress passed the USA PATRIOT Act, dramatically expanding government surveillance powers in the name of counterterrorism. The law authorized sweeping domestic intelligence gathering and became a defining pillar of the post-9/11 security state.

title: US Invades Iraq
description: The United States led a coalition invasion of Iraq that overthrew Saddam Hussein's government in three weeks. The invasion, premised on false claims about weapons of mass destruction, triggered years of insurgency, civil war, and profound regional destabilization.

title: Abu Ghraib Prison Abuse Scandal
description: Photographs documenting US soldiers abusing Iraqi prisoners at Abu Ghraib prison became public, causing an international outcry. The scandal severely damaged America's reputation, became a major insurgent recruitment tool, and triggered a national debate on torture policy.

title: Hurricane Katrina — Catastrophic Federal Response Failure
description: Hurricane Katrina overwhelmed the New Orleans levees, flooding 80 percent of the city and killing over 1,800 people. The catastrophic failure of federal emergency management exposed deep racial and class inequities and severely damaged the Bush presidency.

title: Iraq Surge Strategy Announced
description: President Bush announced a surge of 20,000 additional US troops to Iraq combined with a new counterinsurgency strategy under General Petraeus. The surge reduced violence significantly and temporarily stabilized Iraq.

title: Financial Crisis — Lehman Collapse and TARP Bailout
description: Investment bank Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy in September 2008, triggering a global financial meltdown. Congress responded with the $700 billion TARP bailout — the largest government intervention in financial markets since the Great Depression.

title: Barack Obama Elected First Black President
description: Illinois Senator Barack Obama defeated Republican John McCain to become the first African American president. His election was a historic milestone in the nation's racial history and reshaped American politics around a coalition of minorities, young, and urban voters.

title: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act Passed
description: President Obama signed the $787 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, the largest fiscal stimulus in US history, to combat the Great Recession. The stimulus stabilized the economy but was politically divisive and sparked the Tea Party backlash.

title: Affordable Care Act Signed — Obamacare
description: President Obama signed the Affordable Care Act, the most sweeping overhaul of American healthcare since Medicare, extending insurance to over 20 million Americans. The law reshaped American political debate and became the defining domestic policy achievement of the Obama presidency.

title: Dodd-Frank Financial Reform Enacted
description: Congress passed the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act, the most comprehensive financial regulation reform since the 1930s. The law created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and imposed new oversight on systemically important financial institutions.

title: Osama bin Laden Killed in Pakistan
description: US Navy SEALs raided a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, and killed Al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden. The operation was the culmination of a decade-long manhunt and a defining achievement of America's post-9/11 counterterrorism strategy.

title: Snowden NSA Surveillance Revelations
description: Former NSA contractor Edward Snowden leaked classified documents revealing the scope of US government surveillance of citizens' communications and foreign leaders. The revelations triggered a global debate about state power, privacy, and the boundaries of counterterrorism.

title: Supreme Court Legalizes Same-Sex Marriage Nationally
description: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in Obergefell v. Hodges that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry in all 50 states. The decision was a landmark civil rights victory, culminating a decade of rapid legal and social change.

title: Iran Nuclear Deal Signed
description: The United States and world powers reached the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action with Iran, limiting Iran's nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief. The deal was a signature achievement of Obama's foreign policy, later withdrawn by Trump.

title: Trump Elected President — Political Realignment
description: Donald Trump defeated former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton in a stunning presidential upset, winning the Electoral College while losing the popular vote. The election marked a decisive break from post-Cold War foreign policy consensus and triggered years of political turbulence.

title: Trump Withdraws from Paris Climate Agreement
description: President Trump announced US withdrawal from the Paris Climate Agreement, calling it unfair to American workers. The decision isolated the United States internationally on climate policy and was reversed by Biden in 2021 before Trump withdrew again in 2025.

title: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act Signed
description: President Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, cutting the corporate tax rate from 35 to 21 percent and reducing individual income taxes. The legislation added an estimated $1.5 trillion to the deficit and was the most significant tax reform since Reagan.

title: Trump Withdraws from Iran Nuclear Deal
description: President Trump withdrew the United States from the Iran nuclear deal and re-imposed harsh sanctions. The decision isolated the US from European allies and accelerated Iran's nuclear enrichment activities.

title: Trade War with China Escalates
description: The Trump administration imposed tariffs on $250 billion in Chinese goods; China retaliated with tariffs on American exports. The trade war disrupted global supply chains, raised consumer prices, and marked a fundamental shift in US-China economic relations.

title: Trump Impeached for First Time — Ukraine Affair
description: The House impeached President Trump on charges of abuse of power and obstruction of Congress related to his withholding of military aid to Ukraine to pressure an investigation of Joe Biden. The Senate acquitted him in February 2020.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic — CARES Act and Operation Warp Speed
description: The COVID-19 pandemic killed over 375,000 Americans in 2020, triggering the worst economic contraction since the Great Depression. The US response included the $2.2 trillion CARES Act and Operation Warp Speed, which produced authorized vaccines in under a year.

title: Biden Defeats Trump — Record Turnout Election
description: Former Vice President Joe Biden defeated President Trump, winning 306 electoral votes and over 81 million popular votes, the most in US history. Trump refused to concede and contested the results, setting the stage for the January 6 Capitol attack.

title: January 6 Capitol Insurrection
description: Trump supporters stormed the US Capitol while Congress was certifying the 2020 election results, resulting in multiple deaths and over 140 officers injured. The attack was the first breach of the Capitol since 1814 and led to Trump's second impeachment.

title: US Withdraws from Afghanistan — Taliban Returns
description: The United States completed its military withdrawal from Afghanistan in August 2021, ending America's longest war at nearly 20 years. The Taliban rapidly seized control and the chaotic evacuation drew widespread international criticism.

title: Dobbs Decision Overturns Roe v. Wade
description: The Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, eliminating the constitutional right to abortion after 49 years. The 6-3 ruling triggered a wave of state abortion bans and became the dominant political issue of 2022.

title: Inflation Reduction Act — Largest US Climate Investment
description: Congress passed the Inflation Reduction Act, providing $369 billion for climate investment — the largest in US history — combined with healthcare provisions and deficit reduction. The law fundamentally reshaped US industrial and energy policy.

title: CHIPS and Science Act Revives Semiconductor Production
description: Biden signed the CHIPS and Science Act, providing $52 billion to revive US semiconductor manufacturing and $200 billion for scientific research. The law was a strategic response to Chinese technological competition and pandemic-era chip supply chain vulnerabilities.

title: Trump Indicted — First Former President Charged Federally
description: Donald Trump was indicted by a federal grand jury on 37 counts related to mishandling classified documents, becoming the first former US president to face federal criminal charges. He was later indicted three more times across state and federal courts.

title: Trump Wins Presidential Election — Second Non-Consecutive Term
description: Donald Trump defeated Vice President Kamala Harris in the presidential election, winning both the Electoral College and the popular vote. Trump became the first president since Grover Cleveland to win a non-consecutive second term.

title: Supreme Court Rules Trump Has Presidential Immunity
description: The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that former presidents have substantial immunity from prosecution for official acts. The decision significantly narrowed the federal criminal cases against Trump and reshaped legal doctrine on executive accountability.

title: Trump Second Term — Mass Deportation and Immigration Orders
description: President Trump began his second term by signing sweeping executive orders on immigration, including mass deportation operations and attempts to end birthright citizenship. The orders triggered immediate legal challenges and diplomatic friction with Mexico and Central America.

title: US Imposes Sweeping Global Tariffs
description: The Trump administration imposed sweeping tariffs on imports worldwide, including a 10 percent baseline tariff and higher levies on China, triggering global retaliation and significant market turmoil. The measures represented the most aggressive US trade protectionism since the 1930s Smoot-Hawley era.

title: DOGE Created — Unprecedented Federal Workforce Reduction
description: Trump created the Department of Government Efficiency, led by Elon Musk, and eliminated tens of thousands of federal workers through buyouts, firings, and agency eliminations. The restructuring triggered legal battles and raised constitutional questions about executive authority over the administrative state.
